findings.title: Check-first uniqueness guard is unfalsifiable: every example in create_subscription_event_spec.rb passes with conversion_duplicate_exists? deleted
findings.spec_ref: SPEC.md §6 (uniqueness guard BEFORE build, check-first; index is the backstop) + §9.2 + slice requirement 'non-vacuous, dedupe-independent uniqueness examples'
findings.detail: The two guard examples pre-create a conversion row of the OTHER conversion type (dedupe-independent, good), then assert failure?, the message 'Conversion SubscriptionEvent already exists for stripe_subscription_id ...', and count == 1. But if the check-first guard is removed entirely (delete conversion_duplicate_exists? or its call site), both examples still pass byte-identically: the INSERT hits the partial unique index idx_subscription_events_conversion_stripe_sub_id, the method-level rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique fires, and context.fail! uses the EXACT same message string, same failure state, same row count. The spec file's own backstop example proves the masking — it stubs conversion_duplicate_exists? to false and observes identical outcomes. So the backstop is pinned in isolation (delete the rescue and its example raises), but the check-first layer — an explicit §6 requirement ('check-first', guard BEFORE build) — has zero examples that fail when it alone is removed. Same falsifiability-gap class as the four HIGHs from runs 1-3. Minimal fix: in the guard examples, additionally assert the backstop path never runs — e.g. expect(Rails.logger).not_to receive(:error) (the rescue's Rails.logger.error is the backstop's only distinct observable) or assert no save/INSERT is attempted (guard fail! aborts before build).

verified: Optional params merged only when present: event_params[:stripe_subscription_id] / [:amount] each behind a trailing 'if context.<param>.present?'; absent params leave event_params byte-identical to base, so the existing caller log_assigned_free_plan_event (organization.rb:1230-1241, unchanged in diff, still passes organization: self with no new params) gets unchanged dedupe semantics and nil columns. Spec example 'leaves both columns nil when the params are absent' covers it.

Conversion-type uniqueness guard runs BEFORE the 5-minute dedupe and BEFORE build; conversion_duplicate_exists? queries SubscriptionEvent.where(event_type: CONVERSION_EVENT_TYPES).where(stripe_subscription_id: ...) — by stripe_subscription_id alone (no organization scoping), matching the single-column partial index (schema: unique on stripe_subscription_id WHERE event_type IN (2,8)). Guard bails out (return unless) for non-conversion types and absent stripe_subscription_id.

Graceful failure: guard path uses context.fail! (Interactor::Failure swallowed by .call class method — both webhook writer sites and organization.rb use .call, never .call!). RecordNotUnique rescued at method level, logged via Rails.logger.error + ap, converted to the same context.fail! — never re-raised. The only unique index on subscription_events besides this feature's is none (schema shows only the non-unique organization_id index), so the method-level rescue cannot mislabel an unrelated constraint.

D10 style: all bail-outs are 'return unless' guards; no .presence anywhere in the file; the webhook's event-type selection (not this slice) is a full if/else expression; no value-selection early returns added.

5-minute dedupe block byte-identical to base; assigned_free_plan* path unchanged (spec examples assert first-call success, second-call failure with the unchanged 'Duplicate SubscriptionEvent created within the last 5 minutes' message, one row).

Guard-order fix: 'return unless organization' now sits immediately after 'organization = context.organization', above both ap logging lines ('Stripe subscription in good standing?' + ap organization.stripe_subscription_in_good_standing). The nil-organization example is falsifiable: reverting the move restores NoMethodError on nil.stripe_subscription_in_good_standing, which Interactor does not rescue, so 'not_to raise_error' would fail; example also asserts result.success? and SubscriptionEvent.count == 0.

Nothing beyond §6 in app/interactors/create_subscription_event.rb: full base-vs-head compare shows exactly (a) the guard move, (b) two conditional merges, (c) the check-first guard block, (d) the RecordNotUnique rescue, (e) the private conversion_duplicate_exists? predicate. Missing trailing newline at EOF is pre-existing at base (verified via xxd), not introduced.

Tests: spec file exists at spec/interactors/create_subscription_event_spec.rb; uniqueness examples are dedupe-independent (cross-type pre-created rows cannot match the event_type-keyed dedupe where-clause, and the guard message, not the dedupe message, is asserted); around-block sets queue_adapter :test (pipeline rule 31) so the model fan-out fired by create!/save enqueues instead of running Discord/PostHog inline; create_credit_test_organization helper exists (spec/support/ai_credits_test_helpers.rb:21); backstop example is falsifiable for the rescue layer; new-params-persisted example is falsifiable for the merge lines. The check-first layer's falsifiability gap is finding r4-l1-a5-001.

D11 delicacy audit (flag-anything duty): git diff for app/jobs/stripe_webhook_handler_job.rb contains exactly two hunks, both purely additive begin/rescue StandardError blocks appended at the sanctioned §5.2 (invoice.paid main-plan else-branch end, after reset_ai_credits) and §5.3 (subscription.deleted else-branch end, after EngagementReport::GeneratorJob, with the plain 'if organization' conditional) insertion points; no if/else reordering, no attribute-access changes, nothing else in the file. Nothing to flag.
